findings.reason: the section would change a shared remedy to name one of two causes, so the instruction must be scoped to the case where the new record proves the pointer absent, or dropped in favour of recording what was seen.
findings.text: §13 says "The pane's remedy for this failure names the missing pointer rather than PATH", but the classification it rewrites (`launch-failed`) is produced by one shared except clause, `except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, CrewError)` around `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:3536-3546` calling `_supervisor_spawn_worker`, so a pointer missing at `read_pointer` and a backend whose executable cannot be exec'd are indistinguishable at that boundary; on a genuine spawn failure the pane would say the pointer was missing and send the coordinator to the wrong repair

findings.reason: the section's justification for instrumenting rather than naming the remover is an absence that cannot be tested as stated, and its diagnosis of the cause is not supported by the records it cites, so the node cannot tell a pointer-removal from a failed spawn and should be told to state the log's coverage window and to treat the cause as unproven until the new record shows it.
findings.text: §13 rests "The remover cannot be named from these records" partly on "`admission-verdicts.jsonl` holds no entry for either launch", but that file is trimmed to 1,048,576 bytes on every append (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:60-61,985-987`) and its oldest surviving line reads `"at":"2026-10-23T16:30:09.527323+00:00"` against cited launches at 07:53Z and 14:53Z, so the log covered neither launch's minute and the absence is rotation loss, not a recording gap; the same §13 also asserts the failure text `worker did not spawn: CrewError: no live run '<run>'` as what the attempt ends at launch with, while the only surviving rows for both runs record `launch-failed` with the composed phrase "the launch for backend 'clive' ended with no wait status recorded before writing any stream record (the process exited before any turn); no model was reached" (`_exit_record_end_phrase`, reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1258), which the same code emits for any pre-spawn failure with no wait status

rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — the pane-remedy instruction cannot distinguish the two causes it must name, and the cited "admission-verdicts.jsonl holds no entry for either launch" is a vacuous absence.
